record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: universal obstruction to Fourier-magnitude degree recovery
record.original_question: Does there exist a single map f in C(S^1;S^1), or in VMO(S^1;S^1), such that for every possible summation process, the sums sum_{n in Z} n |a_n(f)|^2 sigma_{n,epsilon} fail to converge to deg f?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.8. Does there exist some f in C(S^1;S^1) (resp., f in VMO(S^1;S^1)) such that for any summation process the series does not converge to deg f?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1 \subset \mathbb{C}$ denote the unit circle. For a measurable map $f: S^1 \to S^1$, let
$$a_n(f) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} f(e^{i\theta}) e^{-in\theta}\, d\theta, \qquad n \in \mathbb{Z},$$
be its Fourier coefficients. For $f \in C(S^1;S^1)$ (or more generally $f \in \mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$, the space of maps of vanishing mean oscillation), the topological degree $\deg f \in \mathbb{Z}$ is well-defined. It is known that, formally,
$$\deg f = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} n\,|a_n(f)|^2,$$
but the series on the right is in general not convergent.

A summation process is, by definition, a family $\{\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}\}_{n \in \mathbb{Z},\, \varepsilon > 0}$ of real numbers such that, for every fixed $n$, $\sigma_{n,\varepsilon} \to 1$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$, and such that for each $\varepsilon > 0$ the weighted series $\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} n\,|a_n(f)|^2\,\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}$ converges absolutely (one may impose mild regularity such as $\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}$ being bounded and compactly supported in $n$ for each $\varepsilon$).

Question: Does there exist a map $f \in C(S^1;S^1)$ (respectively $f \in \mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$) such that for every summation process $\{\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}\}$ one has
$$\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} n\,|a_n(f)|^2\,\sigma_{n,\varepsilon} \neq \deg f$$
(either the limit does not exist or it differs from $\deg f$)?
artifact.status_search_result: Search located the problem within Brezis's published list of favorite open problems and related surveys on VMO degree theory and winding numbers via Fourier series. While a recent complete solution to a different problem ("Brezis' First Open Problem") was found, no source indicates this particular question on universal failure of summation processes has been resolved. Status is therefore inconclusive from available sources.

status_evidence.title: Winding numbers and Fourier series
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of recovering the winding number/degree of S^1-valued maps from their Fourier coefficients via summation processes.
status_evidence.claim: The general question of recovering degree from |a_n(f)|^2 via summation processes is part of an active line of research, with no resolution of the universal-obstruction question reported.
